description: Banner — a tone strip announcing something about the whole view. A tone surface with a subtle tone border (the EDS 2.0 mock, refined), the tone's own icon seated on the first line, a message set for READING and trimmed to the cap box, and an optional dismiss that IS the ghost icon-button, its cap box on the corner. Height is never stated: it emerges from the recipe and grows with a wrapping message.
notes: v0.4.0 (Victor 2026-08-31): STATIC = SURFACE TIER — the strip sits on bg-{tone}-surface (step 2), NOT the interactive muted rung (step 3): Victor found the ghost hover lands on the same step as a muted-default strip (the dismiss IS a ghost button on the banner), so the interactive ladder needs the room above a static tint; the new team minted 'non-interactive' at step 1, which nearly vanishes in dark — surface is the same idea one step safer, and it already exists. Plus the team's nice touch: a SUBTLE TONE BORDER (border-{tone}-subtle, stroke-thin, drawn as an inset outline so geometry is untouched). v0.3.0: READING TEXT SITS ON THE BASELINE GRID — the message rides text-box: trim-both ex alphabetic PLUS padding-top round(1cap,4px)−1ex (Victor's codepen VYmaowY): the occupied box is exactly the ROUNDED cap and the baseline lands on the 4px grid at the box bottom (@supports-gated --eds-text-box/--eds-padding-top-baseline; the fallback keeps the half-leading subtraction — the --_trim-lead/--_baseline-pad pair switches the padding and every glyph seat together). Figma cannot trim: a recorded, bounded divergence — strip heights AGREE at every line count by construction (trim removes exactly the 2×half-leading the padding gains). ICON seats on the FIRST LINE (root align start): with trim, icon cap box top = text cap top = the inset, exactly; Figma mirrors by sizing the icon container to the first LINE BOX (line-height, not cap) and top-aligning. DISMISS IS THE GHOST ICON-BUTTON (composition, not imitation): its own hover plate, focus ring and accessible-name guard come with it; the banner only seats the button's CAP BOX on the upper-right corner — the plate overflows like ink (you only see the circle on hover anyway; Victor). The overhang is the Button's own inset, declared, not assumed. GAP: 16px (spacing-horizontal-md), NOT the icon gap — the icon-label gap is for glyphs beside their label inside an atom; the banner is a CONTAINER (Victor's taxonomy: selectable atoms / containers pad md-16 and gap the same / pages pad xl-24). MESSAGE INK is text-{tone}-strong — almost black, a hint of the tone. Icons stay tone-owned (swapByProp; Icon boolean = visibility only). role=status: banners announce; alert semantics (assertive) are the consumer's call for danger uses.

props.name: tone
props.description: What the banner announces. The tone owns its icon and tints its ink.

props.description:
The announcement — text meant to be read, not scanned. Code: a

props.name: icon

props.name: dismissible
props.description: The ghost icon-button with the close glyph, cap box on the upper right corner (same prop as the chip's).
